source.title: Semantic Sections: An Atlas-Native Feature Ontology for Obstructed Representation Spaces

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports new results that refine the global-feature ontology: in the frozen LLM atlases it studies, section-based identity recovery succeeds where raw cross-chart vector similarity often does not. It does not test the sparse-superposition mechanism or any listed version’s specific claim about capacity, sparsity, SAEs, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The paper measures semantic sections and raw cross-chart similarity in frozen LLM atlases. It does not measure feature sparsity, feature co-activation, capacity competition, interference, neuron polysemanticity, SAE recovery or completeness, or the dimensionality of superposed features. Its reported semantic-section and identity-recovery results are recorded as bearing on the adjacent question of global-vector feature identity, not as tests of any listed version. The paper also states that section recovery is perfect by construction once a candidate is certified as one section.
record.test_reason: The paper argues against a 'global feature' ontology (single directions or dictionary atoms) in frozen LLM context atlases. It does not measure anything any version names: no toy models, sparsity, capacity, neuron polysemanticity, SAE recovery, completeness or stability, or feature dimensionality. Its key comparison sets section membership, which is perfect by construction, against raw cosine between chart-local representatives. Same-object pairs are defined by the paper's own pipeline, so this is not an independent test of V5 or V6. Superposition and SAE work appear only in related work and motivation. The record's 'tests'/T5 contradicts its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author argues that in obstructed atlas regimes a feature is better modeled as a transport-compatible semantic section than as one global vector. Support comes from a cross-model section census and from raw cross-chart cosine failing to recover within-section pairs, while section recovery is perfect on certified supports by construction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses frozen LLM context atlases, seeded propagation, synchronization, defect pruning, cycle classification, and deduplication; it does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition's toy-network experiments or measure sparse-feature interference.
record.method_sensitivity: The section census varies with layer and taxonomy/deduplication thresholds: Llama is measured at layers 12, 16, and 20; a 27-setting threshold sweep reports variation in section counts, particularly the globalizable/twisted partition.

fits_no_version.finding: Deduplicated census of section types differs by model and Llama layer. Gemma layer 16: 14 globalizable, 4 twisted, 8 tree-local, 40 fragile. Llama layer 20 has no cycle-supported sections. Counts shift modestly under a 27-setting threshold sweep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under this atlas pipeline, frozen LLMs yield model- and layer-dependent populations of transport-compatible local feature families with differing cycle consistency.

fits_no_version.finding: Chart-local representatives within a certified section have low raw signed cosine. For Gemma globalizable sections: 19.57% of pairs at 0.3, 2.62% at 0.5, 0% at 0.7. Section recovery is 1.0 by construction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chart-local representatives grouped by atlas transport are not generally recoverable as one identity by raw cross-chart cosine.

record.problems: The experiments use frozen atlas constructions, a fixed discovery budget of 512 seeded discoveries per model for layer-16 runs, and operational thresholds. The paper says its census is not exhaustive. Identity-recovery positives are defined as pairs belonging to the same discovered section, so section recovery is perfect by construction rather than an independent semantic validation. The reported comparisons use selected chart supports; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 type-wise geometric profiles and Table 4 representative profiles were left out because they repeat section counts and exemplar-level geometric details without measuring any listed claim version. Table 5's pairwise cosine and edge/path/holonomy profiles were also left out; the identity-recovery comparisons in Tables 6 and 7 record the directly reported raw-similarity recovery outcomes. Figures are not separately extracted where their results duplicate the tables.

untested.parts: No toy models; no feature sparsity, overlap geometry or phase transition measured.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition measured.
No measure of features spread across neurons; no SAE or dictionary recovery.
No SAE evaluated. The claim that dictionary atoms aren't the right primitive is argued, not measured on SAE features.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features. The paper contrasts single global vectors with chart-local families, not feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The Table 6 and 7 rows compare the paper's own section criterion (1.0 by definition) with a raw-cosine baseline. They are method-versus-baseline rows with circular ground truth, not measurements of a version. Keep them as versions none / cannot_determine. The cosines are between chart-local coordinates of separate local bases, so low cosine may partly reflect basis choice rather than non-global features. 'Control' for Qwen is the paper's own label, not an experimental control. The study builds on the author's own gauge-theory-of-superposition paper (arXiv:2603.00824), which is the one to check for a closer test.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
Neuronal polysemanticity, capacity pressure, feature competition, and dedicated versus shared dimensions are not tested.
The causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition are not tested.
Feature distribution across neurons and sparse features recovered by a dictionary or SAE are not measured.
The completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features is not tested; no SAE is evaluated.
The dimensionality of superposed features is not tested. The paper compares global-vector similarity with atlas-native sections, not one-dimensional with multidimensional features.
